name: Paper Craft / Cardboard Craft
visualIdentity: A tactile paperboard world: visible fibers, thickness, creases, cuts, folds, and assembly seams, with soft light and plausible construction. Explicitly preserve board thickness; do not bend cardboard like rubber.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to tactile assembly and unfolding. The source suggests expressive product reveals, packaging, maker brands, sustainability stories, and explanatory or miniature scenes. These are inferred fits, subject to the constraints below.
limitations: Keep parts connected plausibly and materials consistent. For miniatures, maintain contact, occlusion, crop margins, readable labels, and coherent scale; avoid unexplained floating parts, heavy blur, incompatible materials, or depth that obscures the active hinge. Omit a motion pattern when its subject, assets, or geometry do not fit.
palette: Suggested fallback: background cream #EFE5D2, foreground dark brown ink #47392B, accent kraft #AF8A5D. These are suggestions for new artwork only; exact task, brand, reference, and existing semantic colors take precedence. Keep three discrete colors, preserve material families and asset colors, and do not add gradients or recolor for contrast. Dark brown on cream is the suggested body text pairing; brown ink on kraft is decorative only. Check actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Animate folds at hinges and assembly joints with plausible connections and stable thickness. Optional paper curls must derive from rest geometry and authored progress; they are not physical simulation. Candidate motions include coordinated reversible opening and emergence, restrained depth parallax, chapter handoffs, and story steps, only when the scene supports them. Interactive hover reverses from current progress with focus or tap equivalents; scroll states must work backward. Video uses seekable timeline time, holds, and deterministic direct seeks, never live input.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style treatment. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and explicit audio requirements. Use effects only when they clarify actions; leave room for reading or speech, then check synchronization, intelligibility, balance, and clipping.
assetRequirements: Create thick paperboard geometry, creases, seams, paper materials, and soft lighting; Blender with bpy and Cycles is the recommended style route, with EEVEE noted for faster rendering. Flat scenes can use SVG or Canvas; 3D curling is optional. Prepare suitable cutouts or layered scenes for motion, and keep assets deterministic or baked. Interactive dioramas may use prerendered frames with live accessible headings and hotspots.
combinations: Use alone for tactile assembly. With style-052, shallow dark-ink impressions share the cardboard material and one soft light; avoid deep embossing, metallic bevels, or a second palette. With style-079, use a bounded miniature stage with consistent board scale and visible active hinges. These are source suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Choose visual construction and motion tools from the style and action first; Blender/bpy owns geometry, materials, light, and hinge motion where appropriate. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export pipeline. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Keep rendering and motion logic separate from the pipeline; use seekable deterministic time, inspect representative frames and the full video, and deliver editable source, key-frame sheet, parameters, and render instructions.
